subject: POC: model selection and evaluation plan

Subject: POC: model selection and evaluation plan

Hi Samir / Amelia —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the trial plan: 

Summary of needs (from our call)
- Customer-facing generative assistant for product recommendations and returns flow
- Multilingual support: primary English, coverage for Spanish + French (~10-15% traffic)
- Latency requirement: p95 <= 350ms for typical queries (<=512 tokens)
- Data: synthetic and redacted production prompts + curated evaluation set (we'll share templates)

Proposed success criteria (POC/trial)
1) Functional: 85%+ human-rated usefulness on the curated prompts (3-point scale)
2) Latency: p95 <= 350ms on Redwood Dedicated instance for interactive calls
3) Cost: target unit cost to be below $0.50 per 1k tokens for generation at expected scale (we'll refine after baseline run)
4) Safety/regression: zero critical privacy leaks on test prompts; known edge cases flagged

Model candidates for the trial (recommendation + fallback)
- Primary candidate: Llama 2 13B Chat (open weight) — good instruction-following, solid multilingual baseline
- Alternative: Mistral-Instruct (7B/Chat variants) — faster and lower cost for English-heavy workloads; may need prompt tuning for Spanish/French
- Fallback: quantized Llama 2 7B / OpenLLaMA 3B for degraded capacity or burst routing to keep latency/cost predictable
- Reranking/embeddings: use a multilingual sentence-transformer embedding model for retrieval/rerank steps (if you plan retrieval-augmented workflows)

Evaluation plan
- Phase 1 (Week 0): Share labeled test set (50-100 prompts per language) + prompt templates.
- Phase 2 (Week 1): Baseline runs (each model) to collect latency, token counts, and automatic metrics (ROUGE / BLEU-like for structured responses)
- Phase 3 (Week 2): Human review (sample of ~200 responses across intents) for quality and safety
- Decision: pick model variant to extend trial to production pilot by end of Week 3

Owners and roles
- BrightRetail: Samir (technical lead), Amelia (procurement / commercial)
- Redwood: Marissa (POC owner / success criteria), Ben (solutions engineer — runtime + infra)

Next steps
1) Samir: confirm the evaluation dataset availability and any privacy constraints by Fri 6/26
2) Redwood (Ben): draft initial cost/latency estimates and provision a Dedicated trial cluster (we can start with 1 GPU + bursting) — target provisioning: week of 6/29
3) Marissa: schedule a 30-min kickoff to finalize model choice and timeline — propose Tue 7/6 10am PT

Attachments: BrightRetail_Requirements.xlsx (requirements + sample prompts).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

2) Fallback behavior: if you route to a quantized 7B model how do you ensure consistent tone/branding? Any recommended prompt templates?
3) Data residency: our legal team flagged that any logs for the POC must be stored in the US and accessible for audits. Can you confirm residency and audit logging?

Subject: Re: POC: model selection and evaluation plan — technical notes

Hi Samir — quick answers and a few technical notes. Happy to go deeper in the kickoff.

Multilingual behavior
- Llama 2 13B Chat generally has reasonable multilingual capabilities for Spanish; out-of-the-box it's decent but prompt tuning or a small supervised fine-tune will improve accuracy on domain-specific phrasing.
- Mistral-Instruct is excellent for English and lower cost per token; for Spanish we recommend prompt engineering and validation; fine-tuning helps but is optional for the POC if you accept a slightly lower Spanish quality baseline.

Fallback and consistent voice
- Routing: Redwood supports model-routing policies. Primary -> fallback mapping is enforced with deterministic prompt wrappers to preserve voice/tone (we add a standard system prompt + slot for brand guidelines).
- For degraded capacity we recommend quantized Llama 2 7B with the same system prompt and a short style guideline (2–3 bullets) to reduce drift.

Residency and logging
- POC trial on Redwood Dedicated in us-west will keep logs in the US. We can enable audit logging and give your security team read-only access to the log exports. We'll provide a SOC2 artifacts packet during the trial.

Performance and cost (ballpark)
- Baseline (Llama 2 13B Chat) on a single A100-like GPU: interactive p95 ~200–350ms for <=512-token responses depending on batching.
- Mistral-Instruct 7B: less memory, p95 ~120–220ms, lower cost.
- Cost estimate (generation only, rough): Llama2-13B: $0.40–0.70 per 1k tokens; Mistral-7B: $0.15–0.35 per 1k tokens. We'll run your sample prompts to refine these numbers.

Attachments: SLA_Draft.pdf (initial SLA we typically use for Dedicated POCs).

Test harness
- I've pushed a simple test harness you can run against the trial endpoint: https://drive.google.com/fake-link/brightretail-poc-plan (contains runbook and scoring template).

Happy to provision the trial Dedicated cluster once we get your confirmation on dataset access and PO.
